title: Claude Code vs Claude Chat
content: Claude Chat runs on Anthropic's servers and can only see what you type or share in the chat box. Claude Code runs on your machine, allowing it to open files and execute commands. Claude Code can be accessed through three methods: terminal, IDE like VS Code, or desktop app. Once open, prompts are the messages sent to Claude, which can be short or very specific.
raw_text: all by itself. You probably already use Claude Chat, the classic one in your browser. You ask it questions, it gives you answers. But what makes Claude Code more powerful than Claude Chat? The answer is where it runs. Claude Chat runs on Anthropic's servers. It can only see what you type or share into the chat box. Claude Code runs on your machine. That's why it can open your files and execute commands. >> >> And that's pretty cool. So how do you actually open it? There are three ways. Your terminal, your IDE like VS Code, or the desktop app. No matter which one you pick, it's the same Claude Code running behind. Now that it's open running, time to talk to it. Prompts. Prompts are the messages you send to Claude. They can be super short like fix this bug, or really long and specific like this.
